title: 1952 AHSME Problem 35
statement: With a rational denominator, the expression \(\dfrac{\sqrt2}{\sqrt2+\sqrt3-\sqrt5}\) is equivalent to:

solutions.text:
Multiply first by the conjugate \(\sqrt2+\sqrt3+\sqrt5.\) This gives \[ \begin{aligned} &\frac{\sqrt2(\sqrt2+\sqrt3+\sqrt5)} {(\sqrt2+\sqrt3)^2-5}\\ &\qquad=\frac{2+\sqrt6+\sqrt{10}}{2\sqrt6}. \end{aligned} \] Multiplying numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt6\) yields \[ \begin{gathered} \frac{2\sqrt6+6+\sqrt{60}}{12} \\ =\frac{3+\sqrt6+\sqrt{15}}6. \end{gathered} \]

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: First treat the denominator as \((\sqrt2+\sqrt3)-\sqrt5\) and multiply by its conjugate
After the first rationalization, a denominator containing \(\sqrt6\) remains; use another conjugate
